issues.legal_issue: A person interested in one specifically identified parcel cannot challenge an acquisition notification on the ground that another parcel included in it was ineligible for dispensing with the objection inquiry when the owner of that other parcel has not challenged the acquisition.
material_facts: The challenger was a tenant of a plot that was admittedly arable or waste land and therefore fell within the urgency provision.
The same notification included another plot on which a permanent construction stood, and the challenger argued that the acquisition procedure could not be used for that plot.
The owner of the other plot did not challenge the acquisition and accepted compensation.
issues.conclusion: The challenger could not question the validity of the notification on the basis of the alleged ineligibility of the other plot, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 17(1) and 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, the objection inquiry under section 5A could be dispensed with for the challenger's arable or waste land. The owner of the other plot was the person entitled to object to dispensing with the inquiry for that plot; because that owner did not challenge the acquisition, the challenger could not do so on the owner's behalf. Sarju Prasad v. State of U.P. (AIR 1965 SC 1763) was distinguished: there, the challenger was entitled to object, whereas here the alleged defect concerned land in which the challenger had no relevant interest.

predicates.acquisition_notification_challenge: The proceeding challenges a notification acquiring land for a public purpose.
predicates.challenger_interested_in_arable_or_waste: The challenger has an interest in a plot that is arable or waste land.
predicates.notice_also_includes_ineligible_other_pl: The challenged notification also includes another plot that is ineligible for the procedure used to dispense with an objection inquiry.
predicates.other_plot_owner_did_not_challenge: The owner of the other plot did not challenge its acquisition.

issues.definition: When a challenger interested in arable or waste land contests an acquisition notification that also includes an ineligible plot whose owner did not challenge, the challenger cannot invalidate the notification based on that other plot.

issues.legal_issue: The persons entitled to object to an acquisition depend on whether the notification identifies particular land or identifies a locality for acquisition.
material_facts: The notification identified particular plots for acquisition rather than notifying a whole locality for acquisition.
The challenger was interested in one of the identified plots and sought to object based on the treatment of another identified plot.
issues.conclusion: When particular land is specifically identified, only a person interested in that land is entitled to object; when a locality is notified for acquisition, a person interested in land within that locality may object to the acquisition of land there.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4(1) and 5A of the Land Acquisition Act must be read together. Section 4(1) permits a locality to be specified, while notifications in practice often identify the particular survey numbers sought to be acquired. The words “as the case may be” in section 5A distinguish an acquisition notification identifying particular land, for which a person interested in that land may object, from one identifying a locality, for which a person interested in land in that locality may object.

predicates.land_acquisition_objection_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an objection to a proposed acquisition of land.
predicates.notification_identifies_specific_land: The acquisition notification identifies particular land to be acquired.
predicates.objector_interested_in_specific_notified: The objector has an interest in land specifically identified for acquisition.
predicates.notification_identifies_locality: The acquisition notification identifies a locality as the area proposed for acquisition.
predicates.objector_interested_in_land_within_local: The objector has an interest in land within the locality identified for acquisition.

issues.definition: An objector interested in specifically identified land, or in land within a locality identified for acquisition, is entitled to object to the acquisition.
